headline: Highest risk is data leakage: cognee handles personal/finance data and can call APIs, while the awesome-production-machine-learning list has no runtime surfaces to constrain or sanitize the pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible injection bridge is documented. agent_a is a non-runnable awesome-list with no io_surfaces, while agent_b is a CLI memory system with session isolation; there is no shared channel or default ingestion path shown between them.
conditions: IF a manual copy-paste bridge is introduced between agent_a content and agent_b prompts, injection risk becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from copy-paste workflows.
Review any pasted content before feeding it to agent_b.
Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from imported text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b explicitly touches personal data and finance data and can call APIs, while agent_a is docs-only and has no runtime egress. The pair still creates a leakage path if agent_b ingests sensitive material from shared docs or outputs it through its API-backed workflow; the blast radius is multiple data classes, not just one file.
conditions: IF agent_b is fed personal data or finance data from a shared workspace, leakage risk is present.
IF agent_b sends retrieved context to an external API, sensitive content can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Restrict agent_b inputs to non-sensitive samples.
Disable or proxy external API calls for agent_b.
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces.
Redact personal and finance fields before ingestion.
requires-engineering: add DLP checks on agent_b outputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has no write or network surfaces and is not runnable, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. agent_b supports multiple instances with session memory, but the pair shows no overlapping write capability or shared mutable target, making conflict unlikely and limited.
conditions: IF both agents are later given write access to the same directory or database, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Keep agent_a read-only as documented.
Avoid assigning agent_b shared mutable resources.
Run agent_b instances in separate sessions.
Document ownership for any future shared workspace.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can surface curated ML resources, and agent_b handles decisions, workflows, and successful implementations. If agent_b treats imported material as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions; the pair lacks a documented verification step, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a-sourced content as authoritative guidance without review, cascading errors can occur.
IF agent_b converts imported recommendations into workflows or decisions, downstream impact increases.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on imported guidance.
Tag imported content as untrusted provenance.
Compare recommendations against a second source.
Limit agent_b to summarization, not execution.
requires-engineering: add provenance tracking between the agents.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while agent_a is a public open-source list with no data handling surfaces. If regulated data is routed into agent_b, compliance obligations depend on its deployment and retention controls; the pair does not prove a breach, but the documented data classes make mismatch plausible.
conditions: IF regulated personal data or finance data is processed by agent_b under a stricter residency or retention regime, compliance mismatch exists.
IF agent_b logs or retains those data classes beyond policy, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Confirm the data classification before use.
Avoid routing regulated data into agent_b.
Review retention settings for agent_b.
Document residency and DPA requirements.
requires-engineering: enforce policy-based retention controls.
